key_insight: The paper argues that token merging should not be guided only by text relevance: some background tokens are also important for preserving image quality. By using diffusion dynamics to decide which tokens to keep, the method aims to speed up generation without losing important visual details.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of choosing which tokens in diffusion-based image generation can be merged safely, so models can run faster while avoiding visible quality degradation.
method: Analyze diffusion dynamics to estimate token importance over the generation process.
Identify tokens that should be preserved even if they are not strongly aligned with the prompt, including important background regions.
Merge redundant tokens more selectively to reduce computation while maintaining image fidelity.
impact: This helps practitioners accelerate diffusion models with a more reliable token-merging strategy that better preserves both foreground and background content. It is useful for practical high-quality image generation where speed and visual consistency both matter.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline showing standard diffusion vs. token-merged diffusion
Heatmap of token importance across foreground and background regions
Flow diagram of token selection: keep vs. merge
Bar chart comparing speedup and image quality trade-offs
paper_title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
paper_authors: SeungJu Cha, Ye-Chan Kim, HyunGee Kim, Sungho Koh, Dong-Jin Kim
